description:
## Why
35 fixtures keep an `.oracle.exs` twin. In 7 of them the only thing Elixir rejects is an fz-only spelling of something the fixture does not test, and the feature behind that spelling is covered by other fixtures.

## What changes
Each is rewritten in Elixir form by the fz-nhb.4 rule (functions in `Main`, `IO.inspect` for `dbg`), headed `# oracle: self`, its twin deleted and its stamp regenerated. Goldens do not move.
- `x % n` -> `rem(x, n)`: 00420, 00569, 00571, 01481 (`%` stays covered by 00189 and others)
- a bare function name as a value -> `&f/1`: 01481
- `List.reverse/2` -> `Enum.reverse/2`: 00793 (01619 still covers `List.reverse/2`)
- `Utf8.valid?/1` -> `String.valid?/1`: 01409 (00503, 00504 cover `Utf8.valid?`)
- `assert/2` lines whose values the golden already prints are dropped: 01494

## Considered and kept (each needs an fz decision first, not a fixture edit)
- 01623: its asserts are the only test of fz-only `String.index_of/2`
- 01582: the only test of fz-only `Kernel.range/3`
- 01625: the only test of fz-only `String.to_byte_list/1`
- 01629: asks for the order through fz-only `Kernel.compare/2` on purpose
- 01634: asserts on fz-only `Process.heap_alloc_stats/0`
- 01129: builds a nested `%Stream{}` by hand; fz `Stream.map/2` merges, so no Elixir spelling reaches the nested reduce
- 01167: unquotes a raw map, which Elixir refuses as invalid AST; `Macro.escape/1` would remove the path under test

## Signal
`ORACLE=check` passes; each of the 7 passes run, interp and build; the tree holds 28 twins.
title: Seven fixtures that spell an incidental feature the fz way are their own Elixir oracle
